title: JPEG marker structure
summary: A JPEG file is a sequence of segments, each starting with a marker: 0xFF followed by a non-zero, non-0xFF byte. Standalone markers (SOI 0xFFD8, EOI 0xFFD9, RSTn 0xFFD0-0xFFD7) have no length. All others carry a 2-byte big-endian length (including the length field itself) followed by that many bytes of payload. Common markers: SOF0 (0xFFC0 baseline DCT), DHT (0xFFC4 Huffman table), DQT (0xFFDB quantization table), SOS (0xFFDA start of scan), APP0 (0xFFE0 JFIF), APP1 (0xFFE1 Exif).

structure.meaning: Payload length + 2, big-endian (only for markers with payload).
Marker-specific data (SOF dimensions, DQT tables, SOS component specs, APP metadata, ...).
After SOS, the entropy-coded segment runs until the next 0xFF 0x00-stuffed or 0xFF (non-zero) marker; 0xFF 0x00 is a stuffed zero.

notes: SOI = 0xFFD8 (start of image), EOI = 0xFFD9 (end of image).
0xFF 0x00 in entropy data is a stuffed zero (not a marker); decoders skip it.
SOF0 (0xFFC0) = baseline sequential DCT; SOF2 (0xFFC2) = progressive DCT.
Restart markers (RST0-RST7, 0xFFD0-0xFFD7) reset the DC coefficient prediction every N MCUs.
JFIF (APP0) and Exif (APP1) are the two common metadata containers.
